newsitem.title: FRANCE: Unions want Trichet questioned on Credit Foncier.
newsitem.headline: Unions want Trichet questioned on Credit Foncier.

text.p: Trade unions at the Bank of France have teamed up with those at Credit Foncier to demand that the central bank's governor Jean-Claude Trichet be called to account publicly for his role in supervising the banking sector at a time when Credit Foncier and others got into trouble.

"He is never questioned about when he was director of the Treasury. There's a kind of reverence, which means that certain questions are never asked directly and publicly," Loik Daguzan, member of the CFDT union at the Bank of France, told Reuters.

"The only place where he is questioned is in the National Assembly finance commission which, unlike in other countries, is done behind closed doors," he said, adding that Trichet should be made to answer in front of the press directly.

Trichet was director of the Treasury from 1987 to 1993, the period in which Credit Foncier and state-owned Credit Lyonnais got involved in risky investments that have since plunged them into difficulty.

A cross-union grouping at the Bank of France, where staff are fighting cutbacks and closure of certain services, has joined with the similar cross-union grouping at Credit Foncier, which is fighting a government shut-down plan, to put their case in a letter to France's National Assembly.
Daguzan said the unions recognised that Trichet was not the only one at the Treasury responsible from keeping tabs on the banking sector during the period in question.
Last summer, when Finance Minister Jean Arthuis announced an inquiry into who was responsible for Credit Lyonnais's troubles, he stressed that Trichet was in no way targeted by the probe.
Some commentators said at the time the issue could destabilise Trichet, but speculation quickly died away and nothing has come of it since.

Meanwhile, unions at Credit Foncier were meeting to prepare a vote by staff later in the day, possibly by secret ballot, on whether and under what conditions they would be willing to release Credit Foncier chairman Jerome Meyssonnier, who is spending his sixth day blocked inside in a staff occupation of the Paris headquarters.
Finance Minister Jean Arthuis added his voice to demands for the release of Meyssonnier on Wednesday and Justice Minister Jacques Toubon said the holding of Meyssonnier was "scandalous."
